mishnayos.summary: Carrying something from inside a house to the street, or from the street into a house, is forbidden on Shabbos. This mishnah shows who is guilty when a poor man outside and a homeowner inside pass something between them.

chunks.he: יְצִיאוֹת הַשַּׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בִּפְנִים,
chunks.en: The ways of carrying out on Shabbos are two, which are really four, for the one inside,
chunks.st: carrying out from a public domain into a private domain or vice versa, which are prohibited on Shabbat, are primarily two basic actions that comprise four cases from the perspective of a person inside a private domain,

words.note: Taking things from one place to another, between a house and the street.

chunks.en: and two, which are really four, for the one outside.
chunks.st: and two basic actions that comprise four cases from the perspective of a person outside, in a public domain. The mishna elaborates:

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. הֶעָנִי עוֹמֵד בַּחוּץ וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת בִּפְנִים,
chunks.en: How so? The poor man stands outside, and the homeowner stands inside.
chunks.st: How do these eight cases take place? In order to answer that question, the mishna cites cases involving a poor person and a homeowner. The poor person stands outside, in the public domain, and the homeowner stands inside, in the private domain.

chunks.he: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ לִפְנִים וְנָתַן
chunks.en: The poor man reached his hand inside and put something
chunks.st: The poor person lifted an object in the public domain, extended his hand into the private domain, and placed the object

chunks.en: into the homeowner's hand,
chunks.st: into the hand of the homeowner.
chunks.stMore: In that case, the poor person performed the prohibited labor of carrying from the public domain into the private domain in its entirety.

chunks.en: or he took something from it and carried it out.
chunks.st: Or, the poor person reached his hand into the private domain, took an item from the hand of the homeowner, and carried it out
chunks.stMore: into the public domain. In that case, the poor person performed the prohibited labor of carrying out from the private domain into the public domain in its entirety.

chunks.en: The poor man is chayav, and the homeowner is patur.
chunks.st: In both of these cases, because the poor person performed the prohibited labor in its entirety, he is liable and the homeowner is exempt.
chunks.stMore: The mishna cites two additional cases. In these, the prohibited labor is performed by the homeowner, who is in the private domain:

words.note: Guilty of breaking Shabbos.
Not guilty.

chunks.he: פָּשַׁט בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֶת יָדוֹ לַחוּץ
chunks.en: The homeowner reached his hand outside
chunks.st: The homeowner lifted an item in the private domain, extended his hand into the public domain,

chunks.en: and put something into the poor man's hand,
chunks.st: and placed the object into the hand of the poor person.
chunks.stMore: In that case, the homeowner performed the labor of carrying out from the private domain into the public domain in its entirety.

chunks.en: or he took something from it and brought it in.
chunks.st: Or, the homeowner reached his hand into the public domain, took an object from the hand of the poor person, and carried it into
chunks.stMore: the private domain. In that case, the homeowner performed the labor of carrying from the public domain into the private domain in its entirety.

chunks.en: The homeowner is chayav, and the poor man is patur.
chunks.st: In both of those cases, because the homeowner performed the prohibited labor in its entirety, he is liable and the poor person is exempt.
chunks.stMore: There are four additional cases where neither the homeowner nor the poor person performed the labor in its entirety, and therefore neither is liable:

chunks.en: If the poor man reached his hand inside
chunks.st: The poor person extended his hand into the private domain

chunks.en: and the homeowner took something from it,
chunks.st: and either the homeowner took an object from his hand and placed it in the private domain

chunks.en: or put something into it, and the poor man carried it out,
chunks.st: or the homeowner placed an object into the hand of the poor person, and the poor person carried the object out
chunks.stMore: into the public domain. In those cases and the two that follow, the act of transferring the object from one domain to another was performed jointly by two people, the poor person and the homeowner.

chunks.en: both of them are patur, because each one did only half.
chunks.st: Because each performed only part of the prohibited labor, both of them are exempt.

chunks.en: If the homeowner reached his hand
chunks.st: So too, in a case where the homeowner extended his hand

chunks.en: outside, and the poor man took something from it,
chunks.st: into the public domain and, either the poor person took an object from
chunks.stMore: the homeowner’s hand and placed it in the public domain

chunks.en: or put something into it, and the homeowner brought it in,
chunks.st: or the poor person placed an object into the homeowner’s hand and the homeowner carried the object into the private domain.

chunks.en: both of them are patur.
chunks.st: Because each performed only part of the prohibited labor, both of them are exempt.

mishnayos.summary: Close to the time of Minchah, a person should not start things that can take a long time, like a haircut or a meal, before he davens. If he already started, he may finish.

chunks.en: A person should not sit down in front of
chunks.st: A person may not sit before

chunks.en: the barber close to Minchah time
chunks.st: the barber adjacent to the time of minḥa

words.note: The afternoon tefillah.

chunks.en: until he davens.
chunks.st: until he recites the afternoon prayer.

chunks.en: A person should not go into the bathhouse, and not
chunks.st: And a person may not enter the bathhouse and may not enter

chunks.en: into a tannery, and not start to eat, and not start to judge a case.
chunks.st: to work in a tannery [burseki]. And he may neither begin to eat a meal nor to sit in judgment until he prays.

chunks.en: But if they already started,

mishnayos.stIntro: After having dealt with the limited and defined topic of the halakhot of carrying out on Shabbat, the mishna begins to deal with the halakhot of Shabbat chronologically, beginning with activities that one may not perform prior to the onset of Shabbat. With regard to one’s daily conduct, the mishna says:

mishnayos.summary: Before Shabbos the Rabbis made rules to keep people from breaking Shabbos by habit, like a tailor carrying his needle or reading by a lamp. The mishnah also gives a similar rule from another area of halacha.

chunks.he: לֹא יֵצֵא הַחַיָּט בְּמַחְטוֹ סָמוּךְ לַחֲשֵׁכָה,
chunks.en: A tailor should not go out with his needle close to nightfall,
in case he forgets and goes out with it on Shabbos.
And a scribe should not go out with his quill.

words.note: A pen made from a feather.

chunks.en: On Shabbos one may not shake out his clothes to get rid of lice,
and one may not read by the light of a lamp.
chunks.explain: He might tilt the lamp to make it brighter.

chunks.en: But in truth they said:
The teacher may look where the children are reading,
but he himself may not read.
In the same way,
a zav may not eat together with his wife, a zavah,

words.note: A man who became tamei with a certain kind of tumah.
A woman with that kind of tumah.

chunks.en: because it can lead to doing a sin.

mishnayos.summary: The Rabbis once gathered in the attic of Chananya ben Chizkiyah ben Garon. When they voted, Beis Shammai had more votes, and they made eighteen new rules that day.

chunks.he: וְאֵלּוּ מִן הַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַעֲלִיַּת חֲנַנְיָה
chunks.en: These are some of the halachos they said in the upper room of Chananya
chunks.st: And these are among the halakhot that the Sages, who went up to visit him, said in the upper story of Ḥananya

chunks.he: בֶן חִזְקִיָּה בֶן גֻּרְיוֹן כְּשֶׁעָלוּ לְבַקְּרוֹ.
chunks.en: ben Chizkiyah ben Garon, when the Rabbis went up to visit him.
chunks.st: ben Ḥizkiya ben Garon.
chunks.stMore: The precise nature of these halakhot will be explained in the Gemara. These halakhot are considered one unit because they share a distinctive element. Since many Sages were there, among them most of the generation’s Torah scholars in Eretz Yisrael, they engaged in discussion of various halakhot of the Torah. It turned out that when the people expressing opinions

chunks.en: They were counted, and Beis Shammai had more
chunks.st: were counted, the students of Beit Shammai outnumbered the students of

chunks.en: than Beis Hillel,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel,

chunks.he: וּשְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר דְּבָרִים גָּזְרוּ בוֹ בַיּוֹם:
chunks.en: and they made eighteen rules on that day.
chunks.st: and they issued decrees with regard to eighteen matters on that day
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the opinion of Beit Shammai.

words.note: Eight and ten make eighteen.

mishnayos.summary: May one start something before Shabbos that keeps going by itself on Shabbos, like soaking ink or dyes? Beis Shammai say only if it finishes before Shabbos; Beis Hillel allow it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we do not soak ink, dyes, and vetch,
chunks.st: One may only soak dry ink in water and dry plants, which produce dyes, in water and vetch
chunks.stMore: for animal food to soften them in water on Shabbat eve, adjacent to Shabbat,

words.note: A plant used for animal food.

chunks.en: unless there is time for them to soak while it is still day.
chunks.st: if there is clearly sufficient time for them to soak for their designated purpose while it is still day,
chunks.stMore: before Shabbat begins, and their continued soaking on Shabbat will have no effect.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit doing so.

mishnayos.stIntro: In this mishna there is a fundamental dispute between Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai: Must one begin refraining from actions prohibited on Shabbat on Shabbat eve? Or, may one initiate an action prior to Shabbat, even if he knows that it will continue on its own on Shabbat itself? These are the details of that dispute:

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai say we may not start heating flax, dyeing wool, or setting traps before Shabbos unless the job finishes while it is still day. Beis Hillel allow it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we do not put bundles of
chunks.st: One may only place bundles of combed flax

chunks.en: flax into the oven,
chunks.st: inside the oven on Shabbat eve if there is sufficient time

chunks.en: unless there is time for them to get hot while it is still day;
chunks.st: so that they will be heated while it is still day.

chunks.en: and not wool into the dye pot,
chunks.st: And one may only place wool into the dyer’s kettle

chunks.en: unless there is time for it to soak up the color.
chunks.st: if there is sufficient time for the wool to absorb the dye while it is still day.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit doing so.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹרְשִׂין מְצוּדוֹת חַיָּה וְעוֹפוֹת וְדָגִים,
chunks.en: we do not spread traps for animals, birds, and fish,
chunks.st: One may spread traps for an animal and birds and fish

chunks.en: unless there is time for them to be caught while it is still day.
chunks.st: only if there is sufficient time remaining in the day for them to be trapped in them while it is still day,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel permit
chunks.stMore: doing so even if there is not sufficient time remaining in the day.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai say that on Erev Shabbos we may not sell to a non-Jew or help him load his donkey unless he can get to a nearby place before Shabbos. Beis Hillel allow it.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we do not sell to a non-Jew, and do not load
chunks.st: One may only sell an item to a gentile on Shabbat eve, and one may only load a burden on his donkey

chunks.en: with him, and do not lift a load onto him,
chunks.st: with him, and one may only lift a burden on him

chunks.en: unless there is time for him to reach a nearby place.
chunks.st: if there remains sufficient time for the gentile to arrive to a near place
chunks.stMore: prior to Shabbat, and the Jew will play no role in the performance of a prohibited labor by the gentile on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel allow it.
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel permit doing so.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai say we may not give skins or clothes to a non-Jewish worker unless the work can be done before Shabbos. Beis Hillel allow all these things as long as the sun is still shining.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we do not give skins to a tanner,
chunks.st: One may not give skins to a gentile tanner,

words.note: A person who makes skins into leather.

chunks.en: or clothes to a non-Jewish laundryman,
chunks.st: nor clothes to a gentile launderer,

chunks.en: unless there is time for the work to be done while it is still day.
chunks.st: unless there is sufficient time for work on them to be completed while it is still day, before Shabbat begins.

chunks.he: וּבְכֻלָּן בֵּית הִלֵּל מַתִּירִין עִם הַשָּׁמֶשׁ:
chunks.en: And in all of these, Beis Hillel allow it while the sun is still out.
chunks.st: And in all of them Beit Hillel permit doing so with the sun,
chunks.stMore: i.e., as long as the sun is shining on Friday.

mishnayos.summary: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says his family gave their white clothes to a non-Jewish laundryman three days before Shabbos. Both Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel agree that we may load the olive press and wine press before Shabbos.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: My father's family used to
chunks.st: The ancestral house of my father, the dynasty of Nesi’im from the house of Hillel, was accustomed to

chunks.en: give white clothes to a non-Jewish laundryman
chunks.st: give its white clothes to a gentile launderer no fewer than

chunks.en: three days before Shabbos.
chunks.st: three days before Shabbat.

chunks.en: And both of them agree
chunks.st: And, however, these, Beit Shammai, and those, Beit Hillel, agree that, ab initio,

chunks.he: שֶׁטּוֹעֲנִין קוֹרוֹת בֵּית הַבַּד וְעִגּוּלֵי הַגָּת:
chunks.en: that we may load the beams of the olive press and the round piles of the wine press.
chunks.st: one may load the beam of the olive press on the olives on Shabbat eve while it is still day, so that the oil will continue to be squeezed out of the olives on Shabbat. So too, one may load the circular wine press
chunks.stMore: to accelerate the process of producing wine from the grapes.

words.note: The olive press, where oil is squeezed out.

mishnayos.summary: We may not start roasting or baking right before Shabbos unless the food can be at least partly cooked while it is still day. Rabbi Eliezer says it is enough for the bottom to form a crust.

chunks.en: We do not roast meat,
chunks.st: One may only roast meat,

chunks.en: an onion, or an egg,
chunks.st: an onion, or an egg

chunks.en: unless there is time for them to roast while it is still day.
chunks.st: if there remains sufficient time so that they could be roasted while it is still day.

chunks.he: אֵין נוֹתְנִין פַּת לַתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה,
chunks.en: We do not put bread into the oven at nightfall,
chunks.st: One may only place dough to bake into bread in the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall,

chunks.en: and not a cake on top of coals,
chunks.st: and may only place a cake on the coals,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּקְרְמוּ פָנֶיהָ מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
chunks.en: unless there is time for its face to form a crust while it is still day.
chunks.st: if there is time enough that the surface of this cake or bread will form a crust while it is still day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says: Enough time so

chunks.en: enough time for its bottom to form a crust.
chunks.st: that its bottom crust should harden, which takes less time.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna enumerates actions that may only be performed on Shabbat eve if the prohibited labor will be totally or mostly completed while it is still day.

mishnayos.summary: Some things may be started right before Shabbos, like putting the Korban Pesach into the oven, and lighting the fire in the Beis HaMikdash. Outside the Beis HaMikdash, a fire must catch well before Shabbos.

chunks.he: מְשַׁלְשְׁלִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח בַּתַּנּוּר עִם חֲשֵׁכָה.
chunks.en: We may lower the Korban Pesach into the oven at nightfall.
chunks.st: one may, ab initio, lower the Paschal lamb into the oven on Shabbat eve at nightfall,
chunks.stMore: so that its roasting is completed on Shabbat if Passover eve coincides with Shabbat eve.

words.note: The Korban Pesach, the Pesach lamb.

chunks.he: וּמַאֲחִיזִין אֶת הָאוּר בִּמְדוּרַת בֵּית הַמּוֹקֵד.
chunks.en: And we may light the fire in the bonfire of the Fire Room.
chunks.st: And one may, ab initio, kindle the fire in the bonfire of the Chamber of the Hearth
chunks.stMore: in the Temple on Shabbat eve, adjacent to the start of Shabbat, and allow the fire to spread afterward throughout all the wood in the bonfire.

words.note: A room in the Beis HaMikdash with a fire to warm the Kohanim.

chunks.en: But in other places, only if there is time for the fire to catch most of it.
chunks.st: And, however, in the outlying areas, meaning in all of Eretz Yisrael outside the Temple, it is prohibited to light a bonfire on Shabbat eve, unless there is sufficient time for the fire to take hold in most of the bonfire, while it is still day.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: with coals, any amount is enough.
chunks.st: With a bonfire of coals, even in the outlying areas one is permitted to light the fire on Shabbat eve at nightfall, even if the fire only spread to any amount
chunks.stMore: of the bonfire. The coals, once they are kindled, will not be extinguished again, and there is no concern lest he come to tend to them on Shabbat.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna cites a list of fuels and wicks that one may not use in kindling the Shabbat lights, either because their use might induce one to perform a prohibited labor on Shabbat or because they are not in keeping with the deference due Shabbat. The mishna begins by listing the materials that one may not use as wicks. That is followed by a list of the substances that one may not use as fuel.

chunks.st: However, one may place the spices

chunks.st: except for an oil lamp that is burning on Shabbat,

mishnayos.stIntro: From a discussion of the halakhot of insulation and preparation for Shabbat followed by a brief tangent dealing with the prohibited labor of cooking on Shabbat, the mishna proceeds to briefly discuss prohibitions relating to set-aside [muktze] items in terms of Shabbat lamps.

chunks.st: nor in salt, nor in lime, nor in sand,

chunks.st: However, one may insulate a pot in them when they are dry.

chunks.st: One may insulate a pot of hot food on Shabbat eve in clothing, in produce,

chunks.st: in doves’ wings, in a carpenter’s wood-shavings,

chunks.st: and in the chaff of fine flax.

mishnayos.stIntro: When a pot is removed from the fire on Shabbat eve it may be insulated in materials that preserve its heat, but not in materials that increase its heat. Raising the temperature of a pot is tantamount to cooking. The mishnayot that follow list those materials in which such a pot may be insulated on Shabbat eve and those materials in which it may not be insulated.

mishnayos.summary: We may wrap a pot in animal skins or in wool, but wool is muktzeh, so we may not move it. The mishnah explains how to take out the pot, and teaches about covering a pot on Shabbos.

chunks.st: and may move

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos our animals must rest, so they may not carry loads into the street. But they may wear things that guard them or help lead them, like a halter or a chain.

chunks.he: בַּמֶּה בְּהֵמָה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
chunks.en: With what may an animal go out on Shabbos, and with what may it not go out?
chunks.st: With what may an animal go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what may it not go out?

chunks.en: A camel may go out with a halter,
chunks.st: A camel may go out on Shabbat with an afsar,

chunks.en: and a female camel with a nose ring,
chunks.st: and a naka may go out with a ḥatam,
chunks.basisNote: The explanations of these words follow Bartenura.

words.note: A special white camel that needs extra guarding.

chunks.en: and a Libyan donkey with a strong bridle,
chunks.st: and a luvdekim may go out with a perumbiya.
chunks.stMore: All these terms will be defined in the Gemara.
chunks.basisNote: The explanations of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: and a horse with a neck chain.
chunks.st: And a horse may go out with a chain around its neck.

chunks.en: And all animals that wear a chain may go out
chunks.st: And, in general, all animals that typically have a chain around their necks when they go out to the public domain may go out

chunks.en: with the chain and be pulled by the chain.
chunks.st: with a chain on Shabbat and may be pulled by the chain. If these chains contracted ritual impurity,

chunks.en: And if the chains become tamei, we may sprinkle on them and dip them in a mikvah right where they are.
chunks.explain: We do not need to take them off the animal first.
chunks.st: one may sprinkle waters of purification on them and immerse them in their place
chunks.stMore: on the animal, and they need not first be removed.

mishnayos.stIntro: Due to the mitzva to rest one’s animals on Shabbat, one’s animal may not go out into the public domain bearing a burden. However, an object designated to protect the animal or to prevent it from fleeing is not considered a burden; therefore, an animal bearing objects that serve that purpose may go out into the public domain. The mishna asks:

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists more things animals may wear on Shabbos, like a donkey's blanket or a cloth on a lamb. Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah limit some of them.

chunks.en: A donkey may go out with a blanket
when it is tied onto it.
Rams may go out with a leather covering tied on.
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of this word follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: Ewes may go out with their tails tied up,
chunks.basisNote: The meanings of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: or tied down, or wrapped in a cloth.
chunks.explain: The cloth keeps a young lamb's wool clean.
chunks.basisNote: The meanings of these words follow Bartenura.

chunks.en: Goats may go out with their udders tied.
Rabbi Yosei forbids all of them,
except for the wrapped ewes.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
goats may go out tied to dry up their milk,
but not to save the milk.
chunks.explain: Then it is tied loosely and may fall off.

mishnayos.summary: Some things an animal may not wear on Shabbos, like a rag hanging from it or ropes tying its legs. We also may not tie camels together and pull them as a line.

chunks.en: And with what may it not go out?
chunks.st: And with what may an animal not go out into the public domain on Shabbat?

chunks.en: A camel may not go out with a hanging cloth,
chunks.st: A camel may not go out with a saddlecloth,

chunks.en: not with its legs tied this way or that way,
chunks.explain: These were ways of tying legs so the camel could not run away.
chunks.st: nor may it go out akud or ragul,
chunks.stMore: which are different ways of tying its legs together, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: and the same for all other animals.
chunks.st: And likewise, tying all other animals in those manners is prohibited. And likewise,

chunks.he: לֹא יִקְשֹׁר גְּמַלִּים זֶה בָזֶה וְיִמְשֹׁךְ.
chunks.en: One may not tie camels to each other and pull them.
chunks.st: one may not tie camels one to the other and pull
chunks.stMore: the lead camel, thereby pulling the others after it.

chunks.he: אֲבָל מַכְנִיס חֲבָלִים לְתוֹךְ יָדוֹ וְיִמְשֹׁךְ,
chunks.en: But he may take the ropes in his hand and pull,
chunks.st: However, he may place the ropes tied to each of the camels in his hand and pull them all,

chunks.en: as long as he does not twist them together.
chunks.st: provided that he does not intertwine the ropes.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists more things animals may not go out with on Shabbos, like a bell or a strap. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah's cow went out with a strap between its horns, but the Sages did not agree.

chunks.en: A donkey may not go out with a blanket
chunks.st: A donkey may neither go out with the saddlecloth

chunks.en: when it is not tied onto it,
chunks.st: when it is not tied to its back,

chunks.en: and not with a bell,
chunks.st: nor with a bell

chunks.en: even though it is stopped up,
chunks.st: even if it is plugged to prevent it from ringing,

chunks.en: and not with a ladder on its neck,
chunks.explain: Wooden bars on its neck kept it from scratching a sore.
chunks.st: nor with a ladder that is around its neck,

chunks.en: and not with a strap on its leg.
chunks.st: nor with a strap that is around its leg.

chunks.en: Roosters may not go out with strings,
chunks.st: And the roosters may not go out with strings

chunks.en: and not with straps on their feet.
chunks.st: and not with a strap on their feet, which are tied there as a sign of ownership.

chunks.en: Rams may not go out with a little wagon
chunks.st: And the rams may not go out with a small wagon

chunks.en: under their tails.
chunks.explain: It kept a long tail from dragging on the ground.
chunks.st: under their tails,
chunks.stMore: as it was common practice to put a small wagon under the tails of grown sheep so that the tail would not be injured by dragging on the ground.

chunks.en: Ewes may not go out with a twig in their nose.
chunks.st: And ewes may not go out ḥanunot,
chunks.basisNote: The meaning of this word follows Bartenura.

chunks.en: A calf may not go out with a small yoke,
chunks.st: nor may a calf go out with a gimon,

chunks.en: and not a cow with a hedgehog skin,
chunks.st: nor may a cow go out with the skin of a hedgehog [kupar],

chunks.en: and not with a strap between its horns.
chunks.st: nor with a strap between its horns. The mishna relates that

chunks.he: פָּרָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
chunks.en: The cow of Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya’s cow

chunks.en: used to go out with a strap between its horns,
chunks.st: would go out on Shabbat with a strap between its horns,

chunks.en: but the Sages did not agree.
chunks.st: contrary to the will of the Sages.

mishnayos.stIntro: This mishna lists additional objects with which an animal may not go out into the public domain on Shabbat:

mishnayos.summary: Which jewelry and hair ribbons may a woman wear outside on Shabbos? The Rabbis forbade some, in case she takes them off to show a friend and carries them in the street.

chunks.he: בַּמֶּה אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה.
chunks.en: With what may a woman go out, and with what may she not go out?
chunks.st: With what items may a woman go out into the public domain on Shabbat and with what items may she not go out?

chunks.he: לֹא תֵצֵא אִשָּׁה לֹא בְחוּטֵי צֶמֶר
chunks.en: A woman may not go out with wool strings,
chunks.st: A woman may neither go out with strings of wool,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְחוּטֵי פִשְׁתָּן וְלֹא בִרְצוּעוֹת שֶׁבְּרֹאשָׁהּ.
chunks.en: or linen strings, or ribbons in her hair.
chunks.st: nor with strings of flax, nor with strips of any other materials that a woman braids in the hair of her head.

chunks.en: And she may not dip in a mikvah with them until she loosens them.
chunks.st: And a woman may not immerse in a ritual bath with them in her hair until she loosens them.
chunks.stMore: When the strings or strips are tight, the water cannot reach her hair unobstructed, invalidating her immersion.

chunks.en: And not with a totefes or with sarbitin,
chunks.st: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with the ornament called totefet, nor with sarvitin

words.note: A band worn across the forehead.
Hair ornaments that hang down.

chunks.en: when they are not sewn on,
chunks.st: that are not sewn into her head covering,

chunks.en: and not with a kavul into the street.
chunks.st: nor with a kavul into the public domain.

words.note: A kind of woolen cap.

chunks.en: And not with a "golden city,"
chunks.explain: A gold crown shaped like Yerushalayim.
chunks.st: And, likewise, a woman may neither go out with a city of gold ornament,

chunks.en: and not with a necklace,
chunks.st: nor with a katla ornament,

words.note: A wide necklace.

chunks.en: and not with nose rings,
chunks.st: nor with nose rings,

chunks.en: and not with a ring that has no seal on it,
chunks.st: nor with a ring that has no seal on it,

chunks.en: and not with a needle that has no hole.
chunks.st: nor with a needle that is not perforated, which are merely for decorative purposes.

chunks.en: But if she did go out,
chunks.st: And if she unwittingly went out wearing any of these,

chunks.en: she does not have to bring a korban chatas.
chunks.explain: These things are not forbidden by the Torah.
chunks.st: she is not liable to bring a sin-offering.
chunks.stMore: According to Torah law, a woman is permitted to go out into the public domain wearing ornaments. However, the Sages decreed that a woman may not go out wearing certain ornaments, lest she remove them to show them to another and inadvertently carry them four cubits in the public domain.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

mishnayos.stIntro: The mishna lists items that a woman may or may not carry into, or wear in the public domain on Shabbat. This depends the particular object is considered an ornament, which she may wear, or merely a burden for the woman, which she may not. Even if it is considered an ornament, there is still concern that she might remove it and carry it in her hand in the public domain, which is prohibited by Torah law.

mishnayos.summary: A man may not go out on Shabbos with some kinds of shoes, tefillin, or armor. If he did, he does not need to bring a korban chatas.

chunks.en: A man may not go out with a sandal full of nails,
chunks.st: A man may not go out on Shabbat with a spiked sandal, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְיָחִיד בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בְּרַגְלוֹ מַכָּה,
chunks.en: and not with one sandal when his foot is not hurt,
chunks.st: And he may not go out with a single sandal when there is no wound on his foot.

chunks.en: and not with tefillin,
chunks.st: And he may neither go out with phylacteries,

chunks.he: וְלֹא בְקָמֵעַ בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִן הַמֻּמְחֶה,
chunks.en: and not with a kamea when it is not from an expert,
chunks.st: nor with an amulet when it is not from an expert,
chunks.stMore: but rather it was written by someone who has not established a reputation as an expert in writing amulets that are effective for those who carry them.

words.note: A written charm worn to help heal.

chunks.en: and not with armor,
chunks.st: And he may neither go out with shiryon,

chunks.en: and not with a helmet,
chunks.st: nor with a kasda,

chunks.en: and not with leg guards.
chunks.st: nor with maggafayim. These terms will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: But if he did go out,
chunks.st: And if he went out into the public domain with any of these,

chunks.en: he does not have to bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: he is not liable to bring a sin-offering.

mishnayos.summary: A woman may not go out with things that are tools or containers and not jewelry, like a needle with a hole or a seal ring. Rabbi Meir says she must bring a korban chatas, but the Sages say some of these are like jewelry.

chunks.en: A woman may not go out with a needle that has a hole,
chunks.st: A woman may neither go out to the public domain with a perforated needle, i.e., a standard needle with an eye,

chunks.en: and not with a ring that has a seal on it,
chunks.st: nor with a ring that has a seal on it,

chunks.en: and not with a kulyar,
chunks.st: nor with a kulyar,

words.note: A kind of headpiece.

chunks.en: and not with a perfume box,
chunks.st: nor with a kovelet,
chunks.stMore: the identity of which will be discussed in the Gemara,

chunks.en: and not with a little bottle of balsam oil.
chunks.st: nor with a flask of balsam oil.

chunks.en: And if she did go out,
chunks.st: And if she did go out into the public domain,

chunks.en: she must bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: she is liable to bring a sin-offering; this is

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: the statement of Rabbi Meir,
chunks.stMore: who holds that in doing so she violated the Torah prohibition of carrying a burden in the public domain on Shabbat.

chunks.he: וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹטְרִין בְּכוֹבֶלֶת וּבִצְלוֹחִית שֶׁל פַּלְיָטוֹן:
chunks.en: But the Sages say she is patur for the perfume box and the bottle of balsam oil.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis exempt one who goes out on Shabbat with a kovelet and with a flask of balsam oil.
chunks.stMore: In their opinion, these are ornaments, and therefore they do not fundamentally violate the Torah prohibition of carrying in the public domain on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: A man may not go out on Shabbos with weapons. Rabbi Eliezer says they are like jewelry for him, but the Sages say they are a disgrace, because one day there will be no more war.

chunks.en: A man may not go out with a sword,
chunks.st: a man may neither go out on Shabbat with a sword,

chunks.en: or with a bow,
chunks.st: nor with a bow,

chunks.en: or with a shield,
chunks.st: nor with a shield [teris],

chunks.en: or with a club,
chunks.st: nor with an alla,

chunks.en: or with a spear.
chunks.st: nor with a spear.

chunks.en: And if he did go out,
chunks.st: And if he unwittingly went out
chunks.stMore: with one of these weapons to the public domain

chunks.en: he must bring a korban chatas.
chunks.st: he is liable to bring a sin-offering.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: they are jewelry for him.
chunks.st: These weapons are ornaments for him;
chunks.stMore: just as a man is permitted to go out into the public domain with other ornaments, he is permitted to go out with weapons.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: they are only a disgrace,
chunks.st: They are nothing other than reprehensible and in the future they will be eliminated,

chunks.en: as it says: "And they will beat
chunks.st: as it is written: “And they shall beat their

chunks.en: their swords into plows, and their spears into pruning tools.
chunks.st: swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks;

chunks.en: A nation will not lift up
chunks.st: nation will not raise sword

chunks.en: a sword against a nation, and they will not learn war anymore."
chunks.st: against nation, neither will they learn war anymore”
chunks.stMore: (Isaiah 2:4). With regard to women’s ornaments, they added that

chunks.en: A garter is tahor,
chunks.st: a garter placed on her leg to hold up stockings is pure
chunks.stMore: and cannot become ritually impure as a utensil,

words.note: A band worn on the leg.

chunks.en: and she may go out with it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: and she may even go out with it on Shabbat. However,

chunks.en: Ankle chains can become tamei,
chunks.st: ankle chains, which were also women’s ornaments, can become ritually impure,

chunks.en: and she may not go out with them on Shabbos.
chunks.st: and she may not go out with them on Shabbat.

mishnayos.stIntro: Just as it is prohibited for a woman to carry out certain items unique to a woman into the public domain, the Sages said that

mishnayos.summary: A woman may go out with a hair piece, a sewn-on ornament, a cotton in her ear, or salt in her mouth for her health. Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi and the Sages argue about a false tooth.

chunks.en: A woman may go out with strands of hair,
whether from her own hair, or from
her friend's, or from an animal's,
and with a totefes or with sarbitin when they are sewn on.
With a kavul or with a wig into the courtyard.
With cotton in her ear, and with cotton in her sandal,
and with cotton she prepared for herself.
With pepper, a grain of salt, and anything
that she puts into her mouth,
chunks.explain: These are for her health or to keep her breath fresh.

chunks.en: as long as she does not put it in for the first time on Shabbos.
And if it fell out,
she may not put it back.
A false tooth or a gold tooth,
Rebbi allows it,

words.note: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi, who wrote down the Mishnah.

chunks.en: and the Sages forbid it.

mishnayos.summary: A woman may go out with a coin tied on a sore, and girls may go out with strings in their ears. Clothes that people normally wear in their country are fine for anyone.

chunks.en: She may go out with a coin on a sore.
chunks.st: may go out with a sela coin that she ties on a wound on her foot.

words.note: A coin.

chunks.en: Little girls may go out with strings
chunks.st: The young girls may go out with strings,

chunks.en: and even with little sticks in their ears.
chunks.explain: These keep the holes in their ears open.
chunks.st: and even with wood chips that are in the holes in their ears
chunks.stMore: so that the holes will not seal. Young girls would have their ears pierced, but earrings were not placed in their ears until they were older.

chunks.en: Arabian women may go out veiled,
chunks.st: Jewish women in Arab countries may go out veiled, with a scarf covering their face,

chunks.en: and women of Madai with cloaks pinned.
chunks.st: and Jewish women in Media may go out with cloaks fastened with stones.

chunks.en: And so may any person,
chunks.st: And, any person
chunks.stMore: in any place is permitted to go out on Shabbat clothed in that way;

chunks.en: but the Sages spoke about what usually happens.
chunks.st: however, the Sages spoke in the present, addressing prevalent situations.

mishnayos.summary: A woman may fasten her cloak around a stone, a nut, or a coin, like a button. But she should not first do it on Shabbos.

chunks.en: She may fasten her cloak on a stone, on
chunks.st: may fasten her cloak on a stone by inserting a small stone and wrapping her cloak around it, as she would with a button. And likewise, she may do so

chunks.en: a nut, or on a coin,
chunks.st: on a nut or on a coin,

chunks.en: as long as she does not first fasten it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: as long as she does not fasten her cloak with them on Shabbat ab initio.

mishnayos.summary: A man without a leg may go out on Shabbos with his wooden leg, says Rabbi Meir, and Rabbi Yosei forbids it. The mishnah also teaches which supports for people who cannot walk can become tamei.

chunks.en: A person missing a leg may go out with his wooden leg.
chunks.st: One with an amputated leg may go out on Shabbat with his wooden leg, as it has the legal status of a shoe;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But Rabbi Yosei forbids it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei prohibits
chunks.stMore: going out into the public domain with the wooden leg, since he does not consider it to have the legal status of a shoe.

chunks.he: וְאִם יֶשׁ לוֹ בֵית קִבּוּל כְּתוּתִים,
chunks.en: And if it has a place to hold soft pads,
chunks.st: And if the wooden leg has a receptacle for pads,
chunks.stMore: a concave space at the top of the leg into which pads are placed to cushion the amputated leg, it assumes the status of a wooden vessel and can become

chunks.en: it can become tamei. His knee supports
chunks.st: ritually impure. And his supports,
chunks.stMore: which are shoes that one who had both of his feet amputated places on his knees in order to walk on his knees, if a zav wears them, they are

chunks.en: can become tamei like something walked on,
chunks.st: subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading.

These supports are vessels designated for treading.

words.note: Tumah of things that a zav steps on.

chunks.en: and he may go out with them on Shabbos,
chunks.st: And one may go out with them into the public domain on Shabbat since they have the legal status of shoes.

chunks.en: and go into the Azarah with them.
chunks.st: And one may enter the Temple courtyard with them.
chunks.stMore: Although, generally, wearing shoes in the Temple courtyard is prohibited, in this regard, the supports do not have the legal status of shoes. However, if one who is crippled to the extent that he cannot walk at all sits on a chair that is attached to him, places supports on his hands, and propels himself along with his hands,

words.note: The courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: His chair and his hand supports
chunks.st: his chair and supports are

chunks.en: can become tamei like something walked on,
chunks.st: subject to ritual impurity imparted by treading.

chunks.en: and he may not go out with them on Shabbos,
chunks.st: And one may not go out with them on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and not go into the Azarah with them.
chunks.st: and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.

chunks.en: Ankatmin are tahor,
chunks.st: Loketamin, which will be explained in the Gemara, are ritually pure
chunks.stMore: in the sense that they cannot become ritually impure because they are not vessels,

words.note: Some kind of wooden supports; the Gemara explains.

chunks.en: but we may not go out with them.
chunks.st: and one may not go out with them on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: Boys may go out on Shabbos with knots that were used as a cure, and princes with bells. Anyone may do this; the Sages just spoke about what was usual.

chunks.en: Boys may go out with knots,
chunks.st: boys may go out on Shabbat with knots as a folk remedy

chunks.en: and princes with bells.
chunks.st: and princes with bells.

chunks.en: And so may any person,
chunks.st: And any person
chunks.stMore: is permitted to go out on Shabbat with those objects;

chunks.en: but the Sages spoke about what usually happens.
chunks.st: however, the Sages spoke in the present, addressing situations that were prevalent.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Meir allows going out on Shabbos with certain things people used as cures. The Sages say these are superstitions of the non-Jews, forbidden even during the week.

chunks.en: We may go out with a locust egg,
chunks.st: One may go out on Shabbat with a locust egg,

chunks.en: and with a fox's tooth,
chunks.st: and with a fox tooth,

chunks.en: and with a nail from a gallows,
chunks.st: and with a nail from the crucified,

chunks.en: to help healing.
chunks.st: for the purpose of healing;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: The Rabbis prohibit using these remedies

chunks.en: it is forbidden even during the week,
chunks.st: even during the week,

chunks.en: because it is a way of the Emori.
chunks.st: due to the prohibition of following the ways of the Amorite.

words.note: A nation that did things of avodah zarah and superstition.

mishnayos.summary: How many korbanos chatas must a person bring if he did many melachos on Shabbos by mistake? It depends on what he forgot: that Shabbos exists, which day is Shabbos, or which melachos are forbidden.

chunks.en: They said a big rule about Shabbos:
chunks.st: stated a significant principle with regard to the halakhot of Shabbat:

chunks.en: Anyone who forgets the whole idea of Shabbos and did
chunks.st: One who forgets the essence of Shabbat,

chunks.st: and performed numerous prohibited labors on multiple Shabbatot,

chunks.st: Anyone who performs a prohibited labor and his labor endures on Shabbat

chunks.st: one who gathers grass,

mishnayos.summary: Writing two letters on Shabbos is a melacha, in any language and in any hand. This is because they marked the boards of the Mishkan with letters to know which ones go together.

chunks.st: whether they were the same letter or two different letters,

chunks.en: whether with two kinds of ink,
chunks.st: whether he did so using two different types of ink,

chunks.en: in any language,
chunks.st: in any language,

chunks.en: is chayav. Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: he is liable. Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.st: One is deemed liable for writing two letters

chunks.en: only because of marking,
chunks.st: only due to marking,

chunks.st: the first person sat in the doorway and filled it,

chunks.st: and a second person came and sat next to him,

mishnayos.summary: Everything needed for the bris milah itself may be done on Shabbos, including putting on a bandage and medicine. Whatever could have been prepared before Shabbos is done in a different way.

If he did not grind the cumin before Shabbos,
he chews it with his teeth and puts it on.
If he did not mix wine
and oil before Shabbos,
each one is put on by itself.
We may not make a covering for it from the start,
but he may wrap a rag around it.
If he did not prepare it before Shabbos,
he wraps it around his finger and brings it,
even from another courtyard.

chunks.he: אֵין תּוֹלִין אֶת הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: we may not hang up the strainer on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not suspend the strainer on a Festival,

chunks.en: and we may not pour into a hanging one on Shabbos,
chunks.st: and one may not place wine for filtering through a suspended strainer on Shabbat;

chunks.en: but we may pour into a hanging one on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: however, one may place wine through a suspended strainer on a Festival.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may strain wine through cloths, and mix a wine drink called anumlin. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Tzadok argue about how much may be made.

chunks.en: We may pour water on
chunks.st: One may pour water over sediment that is in a strainer on Shabbat

chunks.en: the wine dregs so that they will become clear,
chunks.st: so that it will become clear and clean.

chunks.he: וּמְסַנְּנִין אֶת הַיַּיִן בְּסוּדָרִין וּבִכְפִיפָה מִצְרִית,
chunks.en: and we may strain wine through cloths and through an Egyptian basket,
chunks.st: And similarly, one may filter wine through cloths and through an Egyptian basket made from palm leaves. Since these liquids are drinkable even without filtering, doing so does not violate the prohibition of selecting. And likewise,

chunks.en: and we may put an egg into a mustard strainer,
chunks.st: one may place an egg in a mustard strainer
chunks.stMore: in order to separate the yolk from the egg-white,

chunks.en: and we may make anumlin on Shabbos.
chunks.st: and one may prepare anumlin, a wine-based drink, on Shabbat.

words.note: A drink made of wine, honey, and pepper.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: on Shabbos, in a cup;
chunks.st: On Shabbat one may only make anumlin in a small cup;

chunks.en: on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: on a Festival,

chunks.en: in a jug; and on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: in a larger vessel; and on the intermediate days of a Festival, one may even prepare it

chunks.en: in a barrel. Rabbi Tzadok says,
chunks.st: in a barrel. Rabbi Tzadok says: There is no objective principle; rather,

chunks.en: it all depends on the guests.
chunks.st: it is all according to the number of guests;
chunks.stMore: if they are numerous, one may prepare a larger quantity of anumlin.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may not soak or sift things in the usual way, because that is like sorting or making medicine. But we may do it in an unusual way.

chunks.en: We may not soak chiltis in lukewarm water,
chunks.st: One may not soak asafoetida in lukewarm water to prepare a medicinal drink from it;

words.note: A spice also used as medicine.

chunks.en: but one may put it into vinegar.
chunks.st: however, one may place it into vinegar like a standard spice.

chunks.en: And we may not soak vetch
chunks.st: And one may not soak vetches
chunks.stMore: in water in order to separate them from their chaff,

chunks.en: or rub it,
chunks.st: nor rub them by hand so as to remove their chaff.

chunks.en: but one may put it into a sieve
chunks.st: However, one may place them into a sieve

chunks.en: or into a basket.
chunks.st: or into a basket, and if the chaff gets removed, so be it.

chunks.en: We may not sift straw in a sieve,
chunks.st: One may not sift straw in a sieve,

chunks.en: and one may not put it on a high place
chunks.st: and similarly, one may not place it on a high place

chunks.en: so that the chaff will come off,
chunks.st: so that that the chaff blows away in the wind;

chunks.en: but one may take it in a sieve
chunks.st: however, one may take the straw in a sieve

chunks.en: and put it into the feeding trough.
chunks.st: and place it into the trough
chunks.stMore: of an animal, and one need not be concerned if the chaff is removed in the process.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Dosa and the Sages argue about moving hay in front of animals on Shabbos. Everyone agrees we may take food from one animal and give it to another.

chunks.en: We may sweep away food from in front of a fattened animal,
chunks.st: One may sweep hay from before an animal that is being fattened,

chunks.en: and push it to the sides for a grazing animal.
chunks.st: and one may move hay to the sides for an animal that grazes on its own in the field (Rabbeinu Ḥananel);
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura explains this differently; we follow Steinsaltz.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Dosa says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Dosa.

chunks.en: But the Sages forbid it.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis prohibit doing so.

chunks.en: We may take from in front of this animal and put
chunks.st: One may take hay from before this animal and place it

chunks.en: in front of that animal on Shabbos.
chunks.st: before that animal on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: Straw on a bed may be moved only with one's body, unless it was set up for sleeping or as animal food. A homeowner may loosen his clothes press on Shabbos, but not tighten it.

chunks.en: Straw that is on top of a bed:
chunks.st: straw that is on top of a bed, if a person wishes to lie on it,

chunks.en: he may not move it with his hand,
chunks.st: he may not move it with his hand
chunks.stMore: to smooth it, as the straw is set aside for kindling;

chunks.en: but he may move it with his body.
chunks.st: rather, he may move it with his body.
chunks.stMore: Since moving straw with one’s body is not the usual manner, it is permitted.

chunks.en: And if it was animal food,
chunks.st: And if the straw was designated as animal food,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עָלָיו כַּר אוֹ סָדִין,
chunks.en: or there was a pillow or a sheet on it,
chunks.st: or a pillow or sheet was on it,
chunks.stMore: which would clearly indicate that the straw was placed on the bed so one could sleep on it, the straw is not considered set-aside, and

chunks.en: he may move it with his hand.
chunks.st: one may move it even with his hand.

chunks.en: A homeowner's clothes press:
chunks.st: A press which belongs to a homeowner,

chunks.en: we may loosen it, but not press with it.
chunks.st: one may loosen it on Shabbat. This press is used to dry and press clothing after laundering. One loosens it to remove clothing from it. However, one may not press clothing with it on Shabbat. And in the case of a press that

chunks.en: And a launderer's press:
chunks.st: belongs to a launderer,
chunks.stMore: which is made specifically for pressing and requires professional expertise for its operation,

chunks.en: he may not touch it.
chunks.st: one may not touch it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if it was loosened before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If the launderer’s press was loosened somewhat on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: he may loosen all of it and take out the clothes.
chunks.st: he may loosen it completely on Shabbat and remove the garment.

mishnayos.summary: A person may pick up his child even if the child is holding a muktzeh stone. Terumah that became tamei may be moved together with good food.

chunks.he: נוֹטֵל אָדָם אֶת בְּנוֹ וְהָאֶבֶן בְּיָדוֹ,
chunks.en: A person may pick up his son with a stone in his hand,
chunks.st: A person may take his son in his hands on Shabbat, and even though there is a stone, which is a set-aside item, in the child’s hand, it is not prohibited to pick up the child.

chunks.en: and a basket with a stone in it.
chunks.st: And it is permissible to take a basket with a stone inside it on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And we may move terumah that is tamei together with
chunks.st: And one may move ritually impure teruma, which may not be eaten and is set-aside,

chunks.en: terumah that is tahor and with chullin.
chunks.st: with ritually pure teruma, as well as with non-sacred produce.

words.note: Regular food that is not holy.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: אַף מַעֲלִין אֶת הַמְדֻמָּע בְּאֶחָד וּמֵאָה:
chunks.en: we may even lift out the terumah from a mix of one in a hundred.
chunks.explain: Terumah mixed into a hundred times as much regular food.
chunks.st: One may even lift a measure of teruma that was nullified from a mixture of one hundred measures of non-sacred produce and one
chunks.stMore: measure of teruma. When a measure of teruma is mixed with non-sacred produce, if the non-sacred produce is one hundred times the measure of teruma, the teruma is nullified. However, the Sages instituted that one must remove an amount equivalent to that measure of teruma and give it to a priest. The remainder is considered non-sacred produce. Rabbi Yehuda permits removing that measure on Shabbat to render the mixture permitted to eat.

mishnayos.summary: We may not lift a muktzeh thing on Shabbos, but we may tip or shake what it is on so it falls off. The mishnah also teaches how to clean a dirty pillow.

chunks.en: A stone that is on the mouth of a barrel:
chunks.st: a stone, which is set-aside on Shabbat and may not be moved, that was placed on the mouth of a barrel,

chunks.en: he tips the barrel on its side and it falls.
chunks.st: one tilts the barrel on its side, and the stone falls.

chunks.en: If it was between other barrels,
chunks.st: If the barrel was among other barrels,
chunks.stMore: and the other barrels might break if the stone falls on them,

chunks.he: מַגְבִּיהַּ וּמַטָּהּ עַל צִדָּהּ וְהִיא נוֹפֶלֶת.
chunks.en: he lifts it, tips it on its side, and it falls.
chunks.st: he lifts the barrel to distance it from the other barrels, and then tilts it on its side, and the stone falls. With regard to

chunks.en: Coins that are on a pillow:
chunks.st: coins that are on a cushion,

chunks.en: he shakes the pillow and they fall.
chunks.st: he shakes the cushion and the coins fall.

chunks.en: If there was bird mess on it,
chunks.st: If there was bird dung (Arukh) on the cushion,

chunks.en: he wipes it with a rag.
chunks.st: he wipes it with a rag,
chunks.stMore: but he may not wash it with water because of the prohibition against laundering. If the cushion

chunks.en: If it was made of leather,
chunks.st: was made of leather, and laundering is not a concern,

chunks.en: we pour water on it until it is gone.
chunks.st: he places water on it until the bird dung ceases.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about how to clear bones and shells from the table on Shabbos. The mishnah also teaches about using a sponge on Shabbos.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: we may lift bones and shells off the table.
chunks.st: One may clear bones and shells left from the Shabbat meal from the table with his hand.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he takes the whole tabletop and shakes it off.
chunks.st: One may remove the entire board [tavla] that is the table surface and shake the bones and shells off of it,
chunks.stMore: but he may not lift them with his hand because they are set-aside and may not be moved.

chunks.he: מַעֲבִירִין מִלִּפְנֵי הַשֻּׁלְחָן פֵּרוּרִין פָּחוֹת מִכַּזַּיִת
chunks.en: We may clear crumbs smaller than an olive's size from the table,
chunks.st: One may clear bread crumbs from the table, even if they are less than an olive-bulk,

chunks.he: וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל אֲפוּנִין וְשֵׂעָר שֶׁל עֲדָשִׁים,
chunks.en: and pea pods and lentil pods,
chunks.st: and pea and lentil pods.
chunks.stMore: Even though it is not fit for human consumption, it may be moved

chunks.en: because they are animal food.
chunks.st: because it is animal fodder. With regard to

chunks.he: סְפוֹג, אִם יֶשׁ לוֹ עוֹר בֵּית אֲחִיזָה,
chunks.en: A sponge: if it has a leather handle,
chunks.st: a sponge, if it has leather as a handle,

chunks.en: we may wipe with it,
chunks.st: one may wipe the table with it,

chunks.en: and if not,
chunks.st: and if not,

chunks.en: we may not wipe with it.
chunks.st: one may not wipe the table with it lest he come to squeeze liquid from it.

chunks.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ,
chunks.en: And the Sages say, either way,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: Both this, a dry sponge with a handle, and that, one without a handle,

chunks.en: it may be moved on Shabbos,
chunks.st: may be moved on Shabbat

chunks.en: and it cannot become tamei.
chunks.st: and it does not become ritually impure.
chunks.stMore: A sponge is not among the substances that can become ritually impure, neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic decree.

mishnayos.summary: If a barrel breaks on Shabbos, we may save food from it, but not soak up the wine with a sponge. We may not squeeze fruit for juice, and the Rabbis argue about juice that drips out by itself.

chunks.en: A barrel that broke:
chunks.st: a barrel of wine or oil that broke on Shabbat,

chunks.en: we may save from it food for three meals,
chunks.st: one may rescue from it food sufficient for three meals,

chunks.en: and he says to others,
chunks.st: and one may also say to others:

chunks.en: "Come and save for yourselves,"
chunks.st: Come and rescue food for yourselves. This applies

chunks.en: as long as he does not soak it up with a sponge.
chunks.st: provided that one does not soak up
chunks.stMore: the wine or oil with a sponge or rag, due to the prohibition of squeezing.

chunks.en: We may not squeeze fruits
chunks.st: One may not squeeze fruits on Shabbat in order

chunks.en: to get juice out of them.
chunks.st: to extract liquids from them.

chunks.en: And if it came out by itself,
chunks.st: And if liquids seeped out on their own,

chunks.en: it is forbidden. Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: it is prohibited to use them on Shabbat. Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if the fruit is meant for eating,
chunks.st: If the fruits were designated for eating,

chunks.en: what comes out of it is allowed;
chunks.st: the liquid that seeps from them on Shabbat is permitted.
chunks.stMore: There is no concern lest one purposely squeeze liquids from fruit that is designated for eating.

chunks.en: and if it is meant for juice,
chunks.st: And if the fruits were originally designated for liquids,

chunks.en: what comes out of it is forbidden.
chunks.st: the liquids that seep from them on Shabbat are prohibited. In the case of

chunks.en: Honeycombs that he crushed before
chunks.st: honeycombs that one crushed on Shabbat eve,

chunks.en: Shabbos, and the honey came out by itself,
chunks.st: and honey and wax seeped from them on their own on Shabbat,

chunks.en: is forbidden. But Rabbi Eliezer allows it.
chunks.st: they are prohibited, and Rabbi Eliezer permits using them.

mishnayos.summary: Salty food that was cooked before Shabbos may be soaked in hot water on Shabbos. Food that was not cooked may only be rinsed, and some salted fish may not even be rinsed, because that finishes cooking them.

chunks.en: Anything that was put in hot water before Shabbos,
chunks.st: Any salted food item that was already placed in hot water, i.e., cooked, before Shabbat,

chunks.en: we may soak it in hot water on Shabbos.
chunks.st: one may soak it in hot water even on Shabbat.

chunks.he: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בָא בְחַמִּין מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
chunks.en: And anything that was not put in hot water before Shabbos,
chunks.st: And anything that was not placed in hot water before Shabbat,

chunks.en: we may rinse it with hot water on Shabbos,
chunks.st: one may rinse it in hot water on Shabbat but may not soak it,

chunks.en: except old salted fish,
chunks.st: with the exception of old salted fish

chunks.en: and small salted fish, and the Spanish kolyas fish,
chunks.st: and small salted fish and the kolyas ha’ispanin fish,

chunks.en: because rinsing them finishes their cooking.
chunks.st: for which rinsing with hot water itself is completion of the prohibited labor of cooking.

mishnayos.summary: We may break open a barrel of figs to eat them, as long as we do not mean to make a vessel. The mishnah also teaches about making a hole in a barrel's plug and smoothing wax.

chunks.en: A person may break the barrel
chunks.st: A person may break a barrel on Shabbat in order

chunks.en: to eat dried figs from it,
chunks.st: to eat dried figs from it,

chunks.en: as long as he does not mean to make a vessel.
chunks.st: provided he does not intend to make a vessel.

chunks.en: And we may not make a hole in the plug of a barrel.
chunks.st: And one may not perforate the plug of a barrel
chunks.stMore: to extract wine from it; rather, one must remove the plug entirely to avoid creating a new opening for the barrel.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

chunks.en: And the Sages allow it.
chunks.st: And the Rabbis permit
chunks.stMore: puncturing the plug, but they too restrict this leniency and say that

chunks.en: But he may not make a hole in its side.
chunks.st: one may not perforate the plug of the barrel on its side.

words.en: shall he make a hole in it

chunks.en: And if it had a hole,
chunks.st: And if it was already perforated,

chunks.en: he may not put wax on it,
chunks.st: one may not apply wax to it to seal the hole,

chunks.en: because he smooths it.
chunks.st: because in doing so he spreads
chunks.stMore: the wax evenly on the barrel and thereby violates the prohibited labor of smoothing.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.en: A case came before Rabban
chunks.st: An incident of that kind came before Rabban

chunks.en: Yochanan ben Zakkai in Arav,
chunks.st: Yoḥanan ben Zakkai in the city of Arav,

chunks.en: and he said, "I am worried that he may need a korban chatas."
chunks.st: and he said: I am concerned for him, because he may be liable to bring a sin-offering as a result of this.

mishnayos.summary: We may put food in a pit to keep it safe, and cold water in the sun to warm it. Someone whose clothes fell in water on the way may keep walking in them and dry them, but not where people see.

chunks.en: We may put cooked food into a pit
chunks.st: One may place a cooked dish into an empty pit on Shabbat

chunks.en: so that it will be kept safe,
chunks.st: so that it will be protected from the heat, and similarly, one may place

chunks.he: וְאֶת הַמַּיִם הַיָּפִים בָּרָעִים בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁיִּצַּנּוּ,
chunks.en: and good water into bad water so that it will cool,
chunks.st: good potable water into a vessel and place the vessel into bad, non-potable water so that the potable water will cool off. And one may also place

chunks.en: and cold water into the sun so that it will get warm.
chunks.st: cold water out in the sun so that it will be heated. They also taught:

chunks.en: Someone whose clothes fell into water on the way
chunks.st: Someone whose garments fell into water while

chunks.en: may walk in them and not worry.
chunks.st: walking on the road may replace them and continue to walk wearing them and need not be concerned
chunks.stMore: about violating the prohibitions against wringing or laundering. When he

chunks.en: When he gets to the outer courtyard,
chunks.st: reaches the outer courtyard of a place where he can leave his clothes,

chunks.en: he spreads them out in the sun,
chunks.st: he spreads them in the sun to dry,

chunks.en: but not in front of people.
chunks.explain: They might think he washed them on Shabbos.
chunks.st: but not opposite the masses,
chunks.stMore: as they will suspect him of laundering on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: Someone who bathes on Shabbos and dries off with towels may not carry them, because he may squeeze them. But ten people who share one towel may carry it, since they will remind each other.

chunks.he: הָרוֹחֵץ בְּמֵי מְעָרָה וּבְמֵי טְבֶרְיָא וְנִסְתַּפֵּג,
chunks.en: One who bathes in cave water or Teveryah water and dries off,
chunks.st: One who bathes on Shabbat in a ritual bath formed by cave water or in the water of Tiberias and dried himself

chunks.en: even with ten towels,
chunks.st: even with ten towels

chunks.en: may not carry them in his hand.
chunks.st: may not carry them in his hand,
chunks.stMore: lest he forget that it is Shabbat and wring the water from them.

chunks.en: But ten people may dry
chunks.st: However, ten people may use

chunks.en: their faces, hands, and feet with one towel,
chunks.st: one towel to dry their faces, hands, and feet,

chunks.en: and carry it in their hands.
chunks.st: and may carry them in their hands.
chunks.stMore: Even though in this case the towel would be quite wet, it is permitted to handle the towel because there are several people present, and they will remind each other that it is prohibited to wring a towel on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may smear oil and rub gently, but we may not do strong exercise or use medical treatments, like setting a broken bone. Someone with a hurt limb may wash it the normal way.

chunks.en: We may smear oil and rub the belly,
chunks.st: One may smear oil on his body and gently rub his body with his hand;

chunks.en: but we may not exercise hard or scrape the oil off.
chunks.st: however, one may not exert himself with vigorous massage or by means of exercise in order to benefit from the therapeutic effects of sweating; and one may not scrape the oil off with a scraper.

chunks.en: We may not go down into a muddy river,
chunks.st: Additionally, one may not go into a swampy river [kurdima], on Shabbat.

chunks.en: and we may not make medicine to vomit,
chunks.st: And one may not make a drug to induce vomiting,

chunks.en: and we may not straighten a baby's bones,
chunks.st: nor may one align a young infant’s bones to straighten them,

chunks.en: and we may not set a broken bone.
chunks.st: nor may one reset a break in a bone.

chunks.en: Someone whose hand or foot came out of place
chunks.st: One whose hand or foot was dislocated

chunks.en: may not shake it in cold water,
chunks.st: may not move them about vigorously in cold
chunks.stMore: water, which is the standard method of treatment;

chunks.en: but he may wash the normal way,
chunks.st: however, one may wash the limb in the typical manner,

chunks.en: and if he gets better, he gets better.
chunks.st: and if one is cured through this washing, he is cured.

mishnayos.stIntro: Apropos the waters of Tiberias, the mishna discusses the halakhot of bathing and medicine on Shabbat.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos a person may borrow wine, oil, or bread from a friend, but not use the word "lend me." If he is not trusted, he may leave his tallis as a promise and settle up after Shabbos.

chunks.en: A person may borrow from his friend jugs of
chunks.st: One may borrow jugs of

chunks.en: wine and jugs of oil,
chunks.st: wine and jugs of oil from another on Shabbat,

chunks.en: as long as he does not say to him, "Lend me."
chunks.explain: That sounds like a business deal.
chunks.st: as long as one does not say the following to him: Loan me.

chunks.en: And so a woman may borrow loaves from her friend.
chunks.st: And similarly, a woman may borrow from another loaves of bread on Shabbat.

chunks.en: And if he does not trust him,
chunks.st: And if the lender does not trust him that he will return them, the borrower

chunks.en: he leaves his tallis with him and makes
chunks.st: may leave his cloak with him as collateral

chunks.en: an account with him after Shabbos.
chunks.st: and make the proper calculation with him after Shabbat.

chunks.en: And so on Erev Pesach in Yerushalayim
chunks.st: And similarly, on the eve of Passover in Jerusalem,

chunks.en: that falls on Shabbos,
chunks.st: when it occurs on Shabbat, one who is procuring a Paschal lamb

chunks.he: מַנִּיחַ טַלִּיתוֹ אֶצְלוֹ וְנוֹטֵל אֶת פִּסְחוֹ,
chunks.en: he leaves his tallis with him and takes his Korban Pesach,
chunks.st: may leave his cloak with him, i.e., the person from whom he is purchasing it, and take the lamb to bring as his Paschal lamb,

chunks.he: וְעוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן לְאַחַר יוֹם טוֹב:
chunks.en: and makes an account with him after Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and then make the proper calculation with him after the Festival.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos a person may count his guests from memory but not from a list. A family may pick lots for their food portions at the table, as long as it is not like a game of gambling.

chunks.en: A person may count his guests
chunks.st: One may count his guests who are coming to his meal

chunks.en: and his side dishes by mouth,
chunks.st: and his appetizers, as long as he does so from memory;

chunks.en: but not from writing.
chunks.st: but one may not read them from a written
chunks.stMore: list, the reason for which will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And he may draw lots with his children and
chunks.st: A person may draw lots with his children and

chunks.en: his household at the table,
chunks.st: family members at the table
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat, in order to determine who will receive which portion,

chunks.en: as long as he does not mean to set
chunks.st: as long as he does not intend to

chunks.en: a big portion against a small one,
chunks.st: set a large portion against a small portion

chunks.en: because that is like gambling.
chunks.st: in such a lottery. Rather, the portions must be of equal size.

chunks.he: וּמַטִּילִין חֲלָשִׁים עַל הַקָּדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: And we may draw lots for the korbanos on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: And one may cast lots among the priests for sanctified foods on a Festival,

chunks.en: but not for the portions.
chunks.st: but not for the specific portions.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may not hire workers or even ask someone else to hire them. We may not wait at the Shabbos border to do a weekday job right after Shabbos, unless it is something we could talk about on Shabbos.

chunks.en: A person may not hire workers on Shabbos,
chunks.st: A person may not hire workers on Shabbat
chunks.stMore: to work for him after Shabbat because even speaking about weekday matters is prohibited on Shabbat. Similarly,

chunks.en: and a person may not tell his friend
chunks.st: a person may not tell another on Shabbat

chunks.en: to hire workers for him.
chunks.st: to hire workers for him.

chunks.en: We may not wait for dark at the Shabbos border
chunks.st: One may not even wait for nightfall at the edge of the Shabbat boundary
chunks.stMore: in order to leave the boundary immediately after Shabbat

chunks.en: to hire workers or to bring fruit,
chunks.st: to hire workers for himself or to bring produce from his field.

chunks.en: but he may wait for dark to guard,
chunks.st: But he may wait for nightfall at the edge of the Shabbat boundary in order to guard his produce that is outside the Shabbat boundary, and he may then

chunks.en: and bring fruit back in his hand.
chunks.st: bring produce back in his hand,
chunks.stMore: since he did not initially intend to wait at the edge of the boundary for this purpose.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul said a rule:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul stated a general principle: With regard to

chunks.en: Anything that I am allowed to say on Shabbos,
chunks.st: anything that I am permitted to discuss on Shabbat,

chunks.en: I am allowed to wait for dark for it.
chunks.st: I am permitted to wait for nightfall at the edge of the Shabbat boundary for its sake.

mishnayos.summary: We may wait at the Shabbos border to take care of a wedding or a funeral right after Shabbos. If a non-Jew does work on Shabbos for a Jew's funeral, a Jew may not use it.

chunks.en: We may wait for dark at the Shabbos border to take care
chunks.st: One may wait for nightfall at the Shabbat boundary to attend to

chunks.en: of a bride's needs,
chunks.st: the needs of a bride

chunks.en: and of a dead person's needs, to bring
chunks.st: and the needs of a corpse, such as

chunks.en: him a coffin and burial clothes.
chunks.st: to bring him a coffin and shrouds. If

chunks.en: A non-Jew who brought flutes on Shabbos:
chunks.st: a gentile brought flutes on Shabbat
chunks.stMore: in order to play music during the eulogy and funeral procession,

chunks.en: a Jew may not use them for a hesped,
chunks.st: a Jew may not eulogize with them as accompaniment,

chunks.he: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן בָּאוּ מִמָּקוֹם קָרוֹב.
chunks.en: unless they came from a nearby place.
chunks.st: unless they were brought from a nearby location
chunks.stMore: within the Shabbat boundary and transporting them did not include any violation of halakha. If gentiles

chunks.he: עָשׂוּ לוֹ אָרוֹן וְחָפְרוּ לוֹ קֶבֶר,
chunks.en: If they made a coffin and dug a grave for a non-Jew,
chunks.st: made someone a coffin and dug him a grave
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat, and they then changed their minds and decided to give it to someone else,

chunks.en: a Jew may be buried in it.
chunks.st: a Jew may be buried in it.

chunks.en: But if it was for a Jew,
chunks.st: However, if it was initially intended for a Jew, a Jew

chunks.en: he may never be buried in it.
chunks.st: may never be buried in it.

mishnayos.summary: We may take care of a person who died on Shabbos, but without moving the body. We may also keep a broken beam from falling more, but not lift it back up.

chunks.en: We may do everything needed for a person who died:
chunks.st: One may perform all of the needs of the dead on Shabbat.

chunks.en: we may smear oil on him and rinse him,
chunks.st: One may smear oil on the body and rinse it with water, and all of this is permitted

chunks.en: as long as they do not move any part of him.
chunks.st: provided that one does not move any of its limbs,
chunks.stMore: which would constitute a violation of the laws of set-aside objects. When necessary,

chunks.en: We may slide the pillow out from under him and lay
chunks.st: one may also remove a pillow from beneath it and thereby

chunks.en: him on the sand, so that he will wait.
chunks.explain: The cool sand keeps the body from spoiling.
chunks.st: place it on cold sand in order to delay its decomposition. Similarly,

chunks.en: We may tie the jaw,
chunks.st: one may tie the jaw of a corpse that is in the process of opening. One may not move it directly so

chunks.en: not so that it will go up,
chunks.st: that it will rise back to its original position,

chunks.en: but so that it will not open more.
chunks.st: but so that it will not continue to open.

chunks.en: And the same with a beam that broke:
chunks.st: And similarly, if one has a roof beam that has broken on Shabbat,

chunks.he: סוֹמְכִין אוֹתָהּ בְּסַפְסָל אוֹ בַּאֲרֻכּוֹת הַמִּטָּה,
chunks.en: we may hold it up with a bench or with the long poles of a bed,
chunks.st: one may support it with a bench or with long poles from a bed. One may not move it so

chunks.en: not so that it will go up,
chunks.st: that the beam will rise back to its original place,

chunks.en: but so that it will not fall more.
chunks.st: but so that it will not continue to fall.

chunks.en: We may not close the eyes of a person who died on Shabbos,
chunks.st: One may not shut the eyes of the dead on Shabbat because the body is set-aside.

chunks.en: and not even during the week while the soul is leaving.
chunks.st: And one may not shut the eyes even on a weekday while the soul departs. One must wait until the person has died.

chunks.en: And one who closes the eyes while the soul is leaving
chunks.st: And one who shuts the eyes while the soul departs

words.en: and the one who closes the eyes

chunks.en: is like a murderer.
chunks.explain: He makes the person die sooner.
chunks.st: is a murderer because he has hastened the person’s death.

mishnayos.summary: If Shabbos starts while a person is still on the road, he gives his money pouch to a non-Jew or puts it on his donkey. When he arrives, he unloads the donkey without carrying muktzeh things.

chunks.en: Someone who was still on the road when it got dark
chunks.st: One who was traveling on Shabbat eve and night fell, and Shabbat began while he was still en route,

chunks.en: gives his money pouch to a non-Jew,
chunks.st: gives his money pouch to a gentile traveling with him.

chunks.en: and if there is no non-Jew with him,
chunks.st: And if there is no gentile with him

chunks.en: he puts it on the donkey.
chunks.st: he places it on the donkey. Once

chunks.en: When he reaches the outer courtyard,
chunks.st: he reached the outer courtyard
chunks.stMore: of the city, where belongings can be securely placed,

chunks.en: he takes off the vessels that may be moved on Shabbos,
chunks.st: he takes the vessels that may be moved on Shabbat off the donkey. With regard to the vessels

chunks.en: and for those that may not be moved on Shabbos,
chunks.st: that may not be moved on Shabbat,

chunks.en: he unties the ropes,
chunks.st: he unties the ropes that attach his bags to the donkey,

chunks.en: and the sacks fall off by themselves.
chunks.st: and the bags of vessels fall on their own.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may untie bundles of food for an animal and spread some of it out. We may not crush hay or carobs for animals, but Rabbi Yehudah allows carobs for small animals.

chunks.en: We may untie bundles of grain in front of an animal,
chunks.st: One may untie peki’in of grain before an animal on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and we may spread out the small bundles,
chunks.st: and one may spread the kifin

chunks.en: but not large ones.
chunks.st: but not the zirin. These terms will be explained in the Gemara.
