chunks.en: We may not crush hay
chunks.st: One may not crush hay

chunks.en: or carobs in front of an animal,
chunks.st: or carobs before an animal
chunks.stMore: on Shabbat in order to facilitate its eating. He may do so

chunks.en: whether a small one or a big one.
chunks.st: neither for a small animal [daka] nor for a large one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah allows carobs for a small animal.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda permits to do so with carobs for a small
chunks.stMore: animal, because it can swallow the hard carobs only with difficulty.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may not overfeed animals or knead their food, but we may put food into their mouths. We give water to animals that need us, but not to bees and doves that can find their own.

chunks.en: We may not stuff a camel with food,
chunks.st: One may not forcibly overfeed a camel on Shabbat

chunks.en: and we may not force food on it,
chunks.st: and one may not force-feed
chunks.stMore: it, even if in doing so he does not overfeed the camel.

chunks.en: but we may put food into its mouth.
chunks.st: However, one may place food into its mouth. And
chunks.stMore: the mishna makes a distinction, which will be explained in the Gemara, between two manners of placing food in the mouths of cattle.

words.en: we put food in its mouth

chunks.en: And we may not stuff the calves,
chunks.st: One may not place food in the mouths of calves on Shabbat in the manner of hamra’a,

chunks.en: but we may put food into their mouths.
chunks.st: but one may do so in the manner of halata.

words.en: we put food in their mouths

chunks.en: And we may feed the chickens.
chunks.st: And one may force-feed chickens.

chunks.en: We may put water into bran,
chunks.st: And one may add water to bran used as animal feed,

chunks.en: but we may not knead it.
chunks.st: but one may not knead the mixture.

chunks.en: We may not put water in front of
chunks.st: And one may not place water before

chunks.en: bees, or in front of doves in a dovecote,
chunks.st: bees or before doves in a dove-cote,
chunks.stMore: because they are capable of finding their own food;

chunks.en: but we may put it in front of geese,
chunks.st: however, one may place water before geese and

chunks.en: chickens, and Herodian doves.
chunks.st: chickens and before hardisian [hardeisiyyot] doves.

words.note: Tame doves that live in the house.

mishnayos.summary: On Shabbos we may cut pumpkins for animals, and meat from a dead animal for dogs. Rabbi Yehudah says if the animal died on Shabbos, it is muktzeh.

chunks.en: We may cut pumpkins in front of an animal,
chunks.st: One may cut the pumpkins before an animal on Shabbat, as long as they were picked prior to Shabbat. And likewise one may cut

chunks.en: and a dead animal in front of the dogs.
chunks.st: an animal carcass before the dogs on Shabbat.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if it was not dead before Shabbos,
chunks.st: If it was not already a carcass, i.e., it was not dead, prior to Shabbat,

mishnayos.summary: Some things may be done on Shabbos, like canceling vows, covering a window, and measuring. The Rabbis learned this from what great people did once to check a roof opening.

chunks.en: We may cancel vows on Shabbos,
chunks.st: may nullify his daughter’s or his wife’s vows on Shabbat,

chunks.en: and ask a Sage about vows that are needed for Shabbos.
chunks.st: and one may request from a Sage to dissolve vows that are for the purpose of Shabbat.
chunks.stMore: Failure to dissolve the vow will compromise one’s fulfillment of the mitzva to delight in Shabbat.

chunks.en: We may stop up a window,
chunks.st: And one may seal a window on Shabbat to prevent light from entering,

chunks.en: and measure a rag and a mikvah.
chunks.st: and one may measure a rag to determine whether or not it is large enough to contract ritual impurity, and one may measure a ritual bath
chunks.stMore: to determine if it contains enough water for immersion. The mishna relates that there was

chunks.st: to ascertain whether or not the roofing had an

chunks.st: opening the size of a handbreadth.

chunks.st: And from their statements and their actions, we derived
